prompt: What makes an object a store?
hint: One method is the whole contract.

choices.text: Being created by `writable` or `readable` from `svelte/store`
choices.why: Those build stores, but the hand-written clock is a store without them.

choices.text: A method called `subscribe` that follows the contract
choices.why: Right. Call it with a function, get called back, get back a way to stop.

choices.text: A `$` at the start of the variable's name
choices.why: The `$` is how a component reads a store, not what makes one.

choices.text: Living in a file whose name ends in `.svelte.js`, so the compiler reads it
choices.why: That is what runes need; `timer.js` is a plain module and its store works.

prompt: Put the life of a subscription to the hand-written `now` in order.
items: The component calls `subscribe` with a function
The store calls that function with `Date.now()` at once
Every 250 ms the interval calls it again
The component goes away and calls what `subscribe` returned
trap: The first value arrives before any interval fires, because the contract says call at once.

prompt: What does the compiler write for you when a component reads `$now`?
hint: Three things you would otherwise do by hand.

choices.text: A copy of the store for this component alone
choices.why: There is one store; the component subscribes to it.

choices.text: A conversion of the store into a `$state` field, kept in step with it by an effect
choices.why: That resembles `fromStore`, which you call yourself; `$` subscribes directly.

choices.text: The subscribe, the variable holding the value, and the unsubscribe when it goes away
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Where does `$now` NOT work?
hint: Which files does the compiler rewrite?

choices.text: In a plain `.js` module, which the compiler does not rewrite
choices.why: Right. Use `get(store)` or `subscribe` there.

choices.text: In the markup of the component that imports it
choices.why: That is exactly where the timer page used it.

choices.text: In the script of a component, at the top level
choices.why: It works there too, for a store imported or declared at the top level.

choices.text: In a component that also uses runes like `$state`
choices.why: Runes and `$store` live together in Svelte 5 components.

prompt: `look … --wait 2400` printed how many seconds on the timer page?
hint: Whole seconds after a wait of 2.4.

prompt: Match each function with the store it makes.
hint: Only one can be set from outside.

pairs.right: A store you set from outside
A store fed by a source it starts
A store computed from other stores

right_distractors: A store that saves itself to disk

prompt: What was wrong with the hand-written clock that `readable` fixes?
hint: Think of two components watching it.

choices.text: It never called its subscriber until the first tick
choices.why: It called `run(Date.now())` at once, as the contract asks.

choices.text: Every subscriber started an interval of its own
choices.why: Right. `readable` keeps one source for all of them.

choices.text: It could not be read with `$` in a component
choices.why: The timer page read it with `$now`.

choices.text: It kept running after the last subscriber had left the page
choices.why: It cleared its interval on unsubscribe; the flaw was having one per subscriber.

prompt: When does the `start` function passed to `readable` run?

choices.text: When the module is imported
choices.why: Importing creates the store; nothing starts until somebody subscribes.

choices.text: Once per subscriber
choices.why: That was the hand-written clock's flaw.

choices.text: When the first subscriber arrives
choices.why: Right, and what it returns runs when the last one leaves.

choices.text: Every 250 milliseconds, as the interval fires
choices.why: The interval calls `set`; `start` ran once to create it.

prompt: Inside a component, `$count += 1` is shorthand for…
hint: The new value depends on the old.

choices.text: `count.update((n) => n + 1)`, from the old value
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `count.subscribe((n) => n + 1)`
choices.why: `subscribe` listens; it never changes the value.

choices.text: `count = writable(count + 1)`, a new store each time
choices.why: That would replace the store and lose every subscriber.

prompt: You start the timer, follow a link elsewhere in the app, then come back by a link. What does `$startedAt` hold?

choices.text: `null`, because the page component was destroyed and created again
choices.why: The component went; the store lives in the module, which stayed.

choices.text: The time it was started, since the module kept it
choices.why: Right. Only a full reload starts it fresh.

choices.text: The time you came back, because the store restarts with its first new subscriber
choices.why: That is `readable`'s source restarting; a `writable` keeps its value.

prompt: Why is the file called `planner.svelte.js` and not `planner.js`?

choices.text: Vite only serves files whose names contain `.svelte`
choices.why: Vite serves `week.js` happily.

choices.text: The compiler only rewrites runes in `.svelte` and `.svelte.js` files
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: It is a naming habit with no effect on how the file runs
choices.why: In a plain `.js` file `$state` would not be rewritten into a signal.

prompt: What does moving `add` and `move` into the class give the planner?
hint: Ask: what can change the planner?

choices.text: Faster updates, because methods skip the proxy
choices.why: They go through the same `$state` fields and proxy.

choices.text: Persistence: a class keeps its state after a reload
choices.why: A reload starts from the data file, class or not.

choices.text: One file where every change to the state is written
choices.why: Right, and a class a test can create with no page.

choices.text: The ability for components to import the same planner without props
choices.why: The component creates its own; a shared instance is the trap of the next section.

prompt: `const { total } = planner;` and then a session is added. What does `total` hold?

choices.text: The old number
choices.why: Right. Destructuring copied it once; read `planner.total` instead.

choices.text: The new number, because `total` is a `$derived` field
choices.why: The field is reactive; the local copy is not.

choices.text: `undefined`, because private signals cannot be destructured
choices.why: The getter returns the value at that moment.

prompt: `Planner.svelte` writes `new Planner(untrack(() => data))`. What would change if `data` were later passed a new value?

choices.text: A new `Planner` would be created with the new data
choices.why: Nothing re-runs the script, and `untrack` says the read is deliberate.

choices.text: Nothing: the planner was made once, from the data as first given
choices.why: Right, which is intended here.

choices.text: The fields would update, because the class reads `data` reactively
choices.why: The constructor copied values out of `data` into its own fields.

choices.text: An error, since a prop read through `untrack` may not change
choices.why: Props may change; `untrack` only stops this read being tracked.

prompt: `bind:selected={planner.selected}` works because the class field is declared with the rune `$___`.
Match each value with the tool the lesson recommends.

pairs.left: A clock that should tick only while watched
An RxJS observable from a library

prompt: You need a store's value inside a `.svelte.js` module. What do you use?

choices.text: `$store`, since the file is compiled by Svelte
choices.why: `$store` is a component feature only.

choices.text: `fromStore(store)`, then read its `.current`
choices.why: Right, as reactive as a `$state` field.

choices.text: `toStore(store)`, which turns it into runes
choices.why: `toStore` goes the other way: runes into a store.

choices.text: Nothing: stores cannot be used outside components in Svelte 5
choices.why: They can: `subscribe` and `get` always work, and `fromStore` exists for this.

prompt: Why is `export const planner = new Planner(…)` in a module dangerous on the server?
hint: How many modules does the server have per visitor?

choices.text: Classes cannot be imported during server rendering
choices.why: They can; the trouble is sharing one instance.

choices.text: The instance is created again on each request, losing changes
choices.why: It is the opposite: the module runs once and the instance is kept.

choices.text: One instance is shared by every visitor's requests
choices.why: Right. The next lesson shows it happening.

prompt: For state an application owns, what does the lesson, and Svelte's documentation, recommend?

choices.text: A `writable` store per field
choices.why: That was the Svelte 4 way.

choices.text: A global object on `window` that every component reads
choices.why: Global state is the singleton trap, made worse.

choices.text: A class or object with runes
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A `derived` store computed from the data file at build time
choices.why: Derived stores compute from other stores at runtime; this is not owned state.

prompt: Which of these are stores? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The hand-written `now` in `timer.js`
choices.why: Yes: it has `subscribe`.

choices.text: `startedAt = writable(null)`
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The `Planner` class
choices.why: No: runes, no `subscribe`.

choices.text: `prefersReducedMotion` from `svelte/motion`, read as `.current`
choices.why: No: it is read through `.current`, the runes way.

prompt: After `--click Start --wait 2400`, the page said `2 s studied`. Which store computed the 2?

choices.text: `now`
choices.why: `now` holds a timestamp, not a count of seconds.

choices.text: `startedAt`
choices.why: `startedAt` holds when Start was pressed.

choices.text: `elapsed`, derived from `now` and `startedAt`
choices.why: Right.
